title: How to Play Sounds on a Website
summary: Plays a drum sound from JavaScript using new Audio and play(), styles each drum button with a background image, and introduces the keyword this to learn which button triggered a listener. Includes three small challenges: play a sound, add button images, and turn the clicked button's text white.

concepts.heading: Finding and understanding a snippet
points: When unsure how to do something, search plainly (e.g. 'play sound javascript'); a Stack Overflow answer shows the pattern: create an audio object and call play on it.
Don't paste snippets blindly. Look up each part on MDN to learn what it does before using it.

concepts.heading: Audio objects
points: new Audio(url) constructs an HTMLAudioElement (a kind of HTMLMediaElement) that points at a sound file. Keep it in a variable.
The path is relative to the HTML page, so a file in the sounds folder is written as sounds/tom-1.mp3 (the reference repo uses ./sounds/tom-1.mp3).
Media elements have properties (e.g. currentTime, paused) and methods; audio.play() starts playback.
Replacing the alert in the click listener with these two lines makes every button play the tom-1 sound. All buttons sound the same until each is tied to its own file (done in the next lesson).

concepts.heading: Challenge: button images
points: The images folder has seven drum pictures (tom1 to tom4, snare, crash, kick). Give each button a background-image in styles.css using url() with a path such as images/tom1.png.

Assign them to the w, a, s, d, j, k, l button classes in whatever order you like (the course uses tom1-4 for the first four keys, then snare, crash, kick), but remember the order so sounds can be matched later.
In the reference repo: .w tom1, .a tom2, .s tom3, .d tom4, .j snare, .k crash, .l kick.

concepts.heading: Identifying the clicked button with this
points: Inside an event listener's function, this refers to the element that triggered the event. console.log(this) prints the button that was clicked.
Because this is the element, its properties are available: this.innerHTML gives the key letter shown on the button, which can later be used to choose a sound.
Flow recap: the loop selects every .drum element in turn and attaches a listener; a click on any one calls the function with this set to that button.
The sound code was commented out while experimenting so only one thing is tested at a time.

concepts.heading: Challenge: change style with this
points: this.style.color = "white" changes the text colour of whichever button was clicked, using the same DOM style property seen in earlier lessons.

task.name: Sound, images and this
task.starting_point: Drum Kit with the click listener loop from the previous lesson (alert inside).
task.goal: Clicking a button plays a drum sound, each button shows a drum image, and the clicked button's text turns white.
steps: Replace the alert with new Audio("sounds/tom-1.mp3") and a call to .play().
Add background-image rules for the w, a, s, d, j, k, l classes pointing at the files in images.
Log this in the listener, click each button and inspect the output.
task.expected_result: Every button plays the tom-1 sound for now, shows its drum picture, and (with the last step) its letter turns white after clicking.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 18 - Advanced Javascript and DOM Manipulation/18.03 - How to Play Sounds on a Website/script.js

pitfalls: Wrong relative path to the sound or image file, so nothing plays or shows (check the folder name and that the extension matches).
(Extra) The reference repo's sounds folder here contains only tom-1.mp3; the full set arrives in the next lessons.
(Extra) Browsers may block audio until the user has interacted with the page; clicks count as interaction.
Using the arrow-function form would change what this refers to; the lecture uses a regular function.

gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'Playing audio and this': tasks: (1) create an Audio and call play(), (2) style buttons with background images, (3) log this in a listener, (4) change this.style.color, (5) show this.innerHTML in a status line.
Interactive demo: buttons that synthesize beeps (Web Audio) so no files are needed, with a panel showing what this is on each click.
